description: Card P's targets for "Highway tractor 15 L": the invariants are hard; the rest are reported, never failed: their misses are the simulator's to-do list. Predicted strongest lines (not measured: the validation format has no line measure yet): the firing frequency, rpm/60 x 6/2, 35.0 Hz at the 700 rpm idle and 101 Hz at the 2014 rpm limiter.

targets.name: Invariant: starts warm and runs
targets.source: a warm engine started on its key runs and keeps running (engine.state 2)

targets.name: Invariant: within full scale
targets.source: 02-contracts.md, section 1: what process writes is within +-1

targets.name: Sound: a free rev is loud enough
targets.source: the lead's ruling (20:11): at a build's defaults a free rev peaks at 0.3 to 0.6 of full scale; under 0.2 is too quiet to hear the work (L's listener at 23 to 30 dB under the reference mix: L's finding)

targets.name: Sound: the idle is audible
targets.source: the lead's ruling (20:11): the idle plainly audible: its level over 8 to 14 s at least -40 dB of full scale (judgement: a quiet room's background against a full-scale peak)

targets.name: Invariant: holds its limiter
targets.source: a diesel's governor holds its high idle, the rated speed plus its 6 % droop (2014 rpm), within a few percent

targets.name: Invariant: pulls away
targets.source: started, in gear and on the pedal, the car moves (a 36 t tractor in third of eighteen at least 1.5 m/s)

targets.name: Invariant: stops at the key
targets.source: the key off stops the engine (engine.state 0 by the run's end)

targets.name: Starts cold
targets.source: a sound engine starts from the air's temperature within some four seconds of cranking and keeps running (a rule of thumb; makers' cold-start specifications are 2 to 5 s)

targets.name: Starts hot
targets.source: a warm engine in 318 K air (a hot day's under-bonnet) starts within some four seconds of cranking and keeps running (judgement, as the cold row)

targets.name: Hot idle
targets.source: the warm engine in 318 K air idles within 100 rpm of the 700 rpm its ECU asks (judgement)

targets.name: Peak power
targets.source: published figures of its kind (the maker's ratings, firm (the range covers its ratings)): 14.9 L; 20 to 30 kW a litre; its full-load fuel curve sets them (D2's, from the class's cited torque through the build's own 8.34 N m a mg): SET BY THE FUEL CURVE, out of the counts

targets.name: Speed at peak power
targets.source: published figures of its kind (the maker's ratings, firm (the range covers its ratings)): 14.9 L: 1600 to 2000 rpm; its full-load fuel curve sets them (D2's, from the class's cited torque through the build's own 8.34 N m a mg): SET BY THE FUEL CURVE, out of the counts

targets.name: Peak torque
targets.source: published figures of its kind (the maker's ratings, firm (the range covers its ratings)): 14.9 L; BMEP 16.8 to 23.4 bar (a naturally aspirated petrol engine 10 to 13 bar, turbocharged 18 to 25, a modern truck diesel 20 to 25: Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 2); its full-load fuel curve sets them (D2's, from the class's cited torque through the build's own 8.34 N m a mg): SET BY THE FUEL CURVE, out of the counts

targets.name: Speed at peak torque
targets.source: published figures of its kind (the maker's ratings, firm (the range covers its ratings)): 14.9 L: 900 to 1300 rpm (a turbocharged engine's plateau: its whole span); its full-load fuel curve sets them (D2's, from the class's cited torque through the build's own 8.34 N m a mg): SET BY THE FUEL CURVE, out of the counts

targets.name: Warm idle
targets.source: makers' service specifications of the kind: 600 to 700 rpm warm in neutral (a rule of thumb, firm to 100 rpm); the ECU is asked for 700

targets.name: Idle steadiness
targets.source: a warm idle's speed wanders some 20 to 50 rpm (a rule of thumb): its highest point from 6 to 14 s more than 100 rpm over the 700 rpm asked is a hunt

targets.name: Idle low point
targets.source: a warm idle's speed wanders some 20 to 50 rpm (a rule of thumb): its lowest point from 6 to 14 s more than 100 rpm under the 700 rpm asked is a hunt (or a stall coming)

targets.name: Boost at its target
targets.source: the build's own target (2.60 bar); a wastegate or vane loop holds a steady full load within some 0.1 bar of its target once spooled (makers' boost-control tolerances; judgement)

targets.name: Charge temperature under boost
targets.source: an air-to-air intercooler of 0.6 to 0.8 effectiveness leaves the charge some 10 to 50 K over the outside air at full boost (makers' and tuners' intake-air-temperature logs; judgement): reported so the over-delivery at a given boost can be judged (the lead's ask)

targets.name: Lambda at full load under boost
targets.source: a turbo diesel at full load runs lambda 1.2 to 2 (smoke-limited; Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 10)

targets.name: Port gas at full load
targets.source: what a thermocouple at a diesel's exhaust port reads at full load (a time mean, below the gas's mass mean: the blowdown is most of the mass and little of the time): some 850 to 1100 K (judgement; Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 14); tel.exhaust.portThermocouple, card G's mixing cup

targets.name: Header gas at full load
targets.source: a thermocouple a little way down a diesel's manifold reads some 700 to 950 K at full load (makers' pre-turbine limits near 1000 K; Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 14); tel.exhaust.headerThermocouple

targets.name: Port gas, mass mean (information)
targets.source: the gas's mass (enthalpy) mean at the port, kept for information: above a thermocouple's reading, not a target (card G, f703892)
